reasons: The cited MFN language runs in our favour: MSL (Vendor) commits to price its engineering to IBM (Customer) on a 'most favored customer' basis, which the rule expressly directs to be marked compliant and not redlined.

Sections 8.2(a)-(b) are a cost-reduction pass-through benefiting IBM, not an MFN obligation on Customer; no obligation for IBM to extend MSL terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers appears in the cited text.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed, and the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs; deterministic checks are empty.
Rationale accurately states the preferred position is met (no MFN burden on Customer, Vendor-granted MFN retained) and is retained as internal evidence rather than a negotiation issue.
